relatedSnapshot.title: Conversations shows which rep sent each message, without opening it
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

In Conversations, every message we send should show which rep sent it, at a glance. Today the rep's name only appears after clicking a text to expand it, so a thread worked by several reps (common under All) reads as if one person sent everything.

## Problem

Setters, closers and payment support all text and call the same people. Opening a conversation under All shows our messages on one side with no name, so a rep can't tell whether they, a setter or an automation sent the last text without clicking each one.

## User experience

* A rep opens any conversation in CRM v2 Conversations.
* Each group of consecutive messages we sent from one sender carries that sender's name (for example "Name 1"), the way group chats label who is speaking. It updates when a different rep, or an automation, takes over.
* Texts, emails and calls all show it: "Name 1" on a text, the sender on an email, and who made or took a call.
* Messages with no known rep read "Name 2" when a workflow sent them, and "Your team" when the sender is unknown, matching today's wording.
* Messages from the contact are unchanged.

## What's included

* The CRM v2 Conversations thread in light and dark, desktop and phone.
* No change to how messages are sent or who is recorded as the sender.

## Done when

- [ ] Every run of our messages shows its sender's name without expanding anything, for texts, emails and calls.
- [ ] A switch of sender inside a thread starts a new label.
- [ ] Name 2 and unknown senders read "Name 2" and "Your team".
- [ ] Checked in light and dark at desktop and phone widths.

## Open questions

* Should the Conversations list row also prefix the last message with the sender ("Name 100: ...")? Recommended default: not in this ticket; revisit after reps use the thread labels.

- [ ] Branched conversations maintain proper message sequencing
- [ ] UI clearly shows conversation branches and allows navigation

relatedSnapshot.title: One canonical AI SDR funnel metric + rebuild the broken admin conversion funnel [NEEDS DEFINITION SIGN-OFF]
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Review corrections (2026-07-16)

These notes supersede any conflicting implementation language below.

Do not call 32.5% canonical until the definition session signs off. Define a cohort using the first qualifying positive event, then count bookings for that same cohort within a fixed attribution window. Report cohort start/end, maturation window, external booking inclusion, deduplication, and timezone. A same-window event ratio is not a true conversion rate.

---

## Overview

Depending on where you look, our positive-reply-to-booked-meeting rate is 4.4%, 23.9%, 32.5%, or 53.1%. None of these is a lie; they count different things, and the 4.4% one is structurally meaningless. We pick ONE definition, rebuild the broken admin funnel on it, and give every surface the same number.

STATUS: needs a 30-minute definition sign-off with James before build. Recommended definition below.

## The prod data (30 days, all measured 2026-07-16)

* Broad-intent positive (distinct threads routed to any non-negative intent) = 17,972 threads; booked via BOOKING_CREATED agent execution = 4,295 (23.9%); booked via lifecycle transition to booked = 5,842 (32.5%).
* 1,542 of the 5,842 booked threads (26%) have NO BOOKING_CREATED execution: scheduling-link/external bookings bypass the booking agent. Agent-based metrics undercount bookings by a quarter.
* The admin funnel (`apps/web/trpc/routers/admin/admin-ai-sdr-v2-analytics.ts`, getConversionFunnel) reports 4.4% because it counts CURRENT lifecycle state filtered by thread.updated_at: ~993k NULL-lifecycle and ~205k stale replied threads merely touched in the window dominate the denominator.
* getIntentDistribution in the same router queries the `intent_classifications` table, which has ZERO rows ever (dead schema); that admin panel renders empty. Intent data actually lives in agent_executions decisions.
* Per-workspace (floor >= 10 positive threads, 437 orgs): p25/median/p75 = 16.7% / 23.8% / 31.9% (agent-booked) or 20.0% / 28.6% / 37.5% (lifecycle-booked); ~32% of orgs clear 30% under the strict definition, ~47% under lifecycle.

## Root cause

1. getConversionFunnel measures the CURRENT lifecycle state of every thread whose `updated_at` falls in the window, instead of counting state transitions that happened in the window. Any old thread that gets touched (webhook, sync, anything that bumps updated_at) re-enters the denominator, so ~1.2M stale/NULL-lifecycle threads drown the real signal and produce 4.4%.
2. "Booked" defined as a BOOKING_CREATED agent execution misses every booking made through a scheduling link or externally (26% of all booked threads), so any agent-based rate undercounts by a quarter.
3. getIntentDistribution reads a table (`intent_classifications`) that no code ever writes to; the intent data it wants lives in `agent_executions` decisions.
4. No canonical definition exists anywhere in the repo, so each surface invented its own; that is why 4.4%, 23.9%, 32.5%, and 53.1% coexist.

## Recommended canonical definition (to sign off)

* Positive = distinct threads whose intent routed to any non-negative intent within the window (from agent_executions).
* Booked = lifecycle_history transition to `booked` within the window (captures external/link bookings).
* Candidate same-window ratio today: 32.5%. This is not canonical until cohort and attribution-window sign-off.

## What to build (after sign-off, one PR)

1. Document the canonical definition in the repo (analytics README) with the exact SQL.
2. Rebuild getConversionFunnel on transitions-in-window (events, not current state). Repoint getIntentDistribution at agent_executions (or wire the dead table, per the observability ticket's decision).
3. Add a per-workspace conversion view to the admin analytics: rate per org, p25/p50/p75, share above 30%, sortable by positive volume.
4. Coordinate with ENG-10978 (Platform Metrics Overhaul): that master owns customer-facing dashboard numbers; this ticket owns the AI-SDR admin funnel. Same definitions, no double implementation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Admin funnel, ad-hoc SQL, and the weekly report produce the same number for the same window
- [ ] External/link bookings included in booked counts
- [ ] Per-workspace view live in admin
- [ ] Definition doc merged

relatedSnapshot.title: Add Intercom conversation export and question extraction scripts
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem Statement

We need visibility into what questions our users are asking via Intercom support tickets to identify knowledge gaps in our help center and track recurring issues.

## Impact Analysis

* **User Impact**: Users repeatedly ask questions that could be answered by help articles, leading to slower resolution times.
* **Development Impact**: No systematic way to identify which documentation is missing or which bugs are most frequently reported.
* **Business Impact**: Support team spending time on questions that could be self-served with proper documentation.

## Solution

Two one-off scripts:

1. `scripts/export-intercom-conversations.ts` — Exports all Intercom conversations with full message history via the Search Conversations API.
2. `scripts/extract-intercom-question-gists.ts` — Processes exported conversations through an LLM to extract core questions, categories, bug/feature flags, knowledge gaps, and suggested article titles.

relatedSnapshot.title: Scheduled folder in Conversations
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The Clock button next to Compose opens a Scheduled folder right inside Conversations, so a rep can browse everything they have waiting, failed, sent or cancelled without leaving the inbox.

## Problem

Today the Clock button leaves Conversations for a separate Scheduled messages page with six status toggles including "Unknown," raw phone numbers instead of names, no message text, and no way back into the conversation.

## Proposed fix

Turn the conversation list into a Scheduled folder in place. Group messages under Upcoming, Failed, Sent and Cancelled, show the person's name, the subject and first line, and who scheduled it, and let a rep edit, cancel or retry right from a row, or click through to that person's thread.

## What's included

* The Clock button switches the conversation list into the Scheduled folder instead of navigating to a separate page; Back returns to the list.
* Header with a "Scheduled" title, an upcoming-count pill, and Mine/Everyone.
* Tabs: Upcoming, Failed, Sent, Cancelled. A message still sending shows a pill on its row rather than its own tab, and one whose delivery is still being checked sits inside Upcoming with a "Checking whether it sent" pill rather than the old "Unknown" tab.
* Rows grouped under day headings, soonest-first in Upcoming and newest-first elsewhere, each with Edit, Cancel and Retry where they apply.
* The old separate Scheduled messages page redirects here, keeping its existing open-tracking.

Not included: the scheduled-count badge on the Clock button itself (ENG-14171, a separate ticket), and anything from ENG-14168 (tasks, meetings, payments on the thread).

## Blocked by

Edit, retry, Remind if no reply and a better Schedule send in Conversations — this folder reuses that ticket's Edit panel and its Retry action rather than duplicating them.

## How it should work

* A rep sees only the scheduled messages, and only the message text, they could already see on today's separate Scheduled page; the folder doesn't loosen any of those checks, it reuses them.
* Upcoming keeps refreshing live the way the current page does; the other tabs don't need to.
* Clicking a row opens that person's thread with its scheduled bubble.

## Who can do what

Same as today's Scheduled page: a rep sees and acts on messages within their existing scope (their own, their team's, or the workspace's, depending on role), and never across workspaces.

## What the user sees

Scheduled becomes a mode of Conversations rather than a separate destination. The open thread stays visible on the right while browsing the folder on the left. The footer states the sort order and the timezone in use.

## Done when

* The Clock button opens the Scheduled folder in place; Back returns to the normal conversation list.
* Upcoming, Failed, Sent and Cancelled show the right messages for the current scope and channel filter, grouped by day.
* Edit, Cancel and Retry work from a row the same way they work from the thread.
* The old Scheduled messages page redirects here and keeps its own open-tracking event.
* The screens match the kit in both light and dark mode.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

A rep can browse, edit, cancel or retry every scheduled message without leaving Conversations, and the old separate page is gone.

## Implementation context

See the linked AI context document for the router change needed for the merged Upcoming view and the exact files this replaces.

relatedSnapshot.title: Reporting (Partner Admin): Funnel conversion rate report
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Company Two needs to see conversion rates by funnel step: opt-in → webinar registration → front-end purchase ($1,500) → back-end upsell ($6K/$10K/$20K). Currently `getExternalTrackingStats` in `affiliate.ts:1065-1134` returns flat totals — total leads, converted leads, total conversions, total revenue. No breakdown by funnel step or product.

## Data available today

The data to build this already exists across three tables:

1. `external_lead_capture` — opt-ins. Has `status` (captured/converted), `capturedAt`, `affiliateLinkId`, `partnerId`
2. `external_conversion` — purchases. Has `productName`, `productId`, `amount`, `source`, `convertedAt`, `partnerId`. This is where GHL/Stripe/manual conversions land with product info
3. `affiliate_link` — click counts per affiliate link. Has `clickCount`

The funnel steps map to:

* **Clicks** → `SUM(affiliate_link.clickCount)` for all links in this partner
* **Opt-ins** → `COUNT(external_lead_capture)` with status = any
* **Purchases by product** → `external_conversion` grouped by `productName` or `productId`

The gap: there's no explicit "webinar registration" event type. This would need to either (a) be a separate `productName` value in external_conversion (e.g. GHL sends it as a conversion with `productName = 'Name 10'` and `amount = 0`), or (b) be tracked as a lead capture with a custom field. For now, we group conversions by product and let the product names define the funnel steps.

## Approach

New tRPC procedure that aggregates funnel steps from the existing tables. New component on a reports page (or the existing analytics page) showing the funnel.

## Changes

### 1\. `trpc/routers/partner-analytics.ts` — new `getFunnelReport` procedure

```ts
getFunnelReport: partnerAdminProcedure
  .input(z.object({
    dateFrom: z.date().optional(),
    dateTo: z.date().optional(),
    affiliateUserId: z.string().uuid().optional(), // filter to one affiliate
  }))
  .query(...)
```

Query logic:

**Step 1 — Clicks:**

```sql
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(click_count), 0) as total_clicks
FROM affiliate_link
WHERE partner_id = :partnerId
  AND (affiliate_account_id IN (SELECT id FROM affiliate_account WHERE owner_user_id = :affiliateUserId) OR :affiliateUserId IS NULL)
```

**Step 2 — Opt-ins:**

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) as total_optins
FROM external_lead_capture
WHERE partner_id = :partnerId
  AND captured_at BETWEEN :dateFrom AND :dateTo
  AND (affiliate_link_id IN (...) OR :affiliateUserId IS NULL)
```

**Step 3 — Conversions grouped by product:**

```sql
SELECT
  product_name,
  COUNT(*) as conversion_count,
  SUM(amount) as total_amount
FROM external_conversion
WHERE partner_id = :partnerId
  AND converted_at BETWEEN :dateFrom AND :dateTo
  AND (attributed_lead_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM external_lead_capture WHERE affiliate_link_id IN (...))
    OR :affiliateUserId IS NULL)
GROUP BY product_name
ORDER BY total_amount DESC
```

Return shape:

```ts
{
  clicks: number;
  optIns: number;
  clickToOptInRate: number;
  conversions: Array<{
    productName: string | null;
    count: number;
    totalAmountCents: number;
  }>;
  totalConversions: number;
  totalRevenueCents: number;
  optInToConversionRate: number;
}
```

### 2\. New component `components/partner-admin/funnel-report.tsx`

Visual funnel display:

* Horizontal or vertical bar/step layout showing:
  * Clicks → Opt-ins → \[Product 1 purchases\] → \[Product 2 purchases\] → ...
* Each step shows: count, conversion rate from previous step
* Optional affiliate filter dropdown at the top
* Date range picker (reuse existing pattern)
* Responsive card layout

### 3\. `app/(saas)/dashboard/(sidebar)/partner-admin/analytics/page.tsx`

Add the funnel report card below the revenue/commission charts (from spec #18). Uses the same `timeRange` state.

Alternatively, if the analytics page gets too long, this can go on a new `/partner-admin/reports` page — but keeping it on analytics is simpler for now.

## Dependencies

* Funnel granularity depends on how Company Two's GHL is configured to send conversions. If GHL sends `productName` for each funnel step (webinar reg, front-end, back-end), the funnel will have that granularity automatically.
* If event type tracking (spec #3) is built first, we could also break down by `eventType` instead of `productName`.

## What this does NOT change

* No DB migration
* No changes to how conversions are recorded
* Existing `getExternalTrackingStats` unchanged
* No new pages (adds to existing analytics)

## Files touched

1. `trpc/routers/partner-analytics.ts` — new `getFunnelReport` procedure
2. `components/partner-admin/funnel-report.tsx` — new funnel visualization component
3. `app/(saas)/dashboard/(sidebar)/partner-admin/analytics/page.tsx` — render funnel report

relatedSnapshot.title: Outlook copies every outside email into the CRM, even with nobody we know on it
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What's happening

When someone connects Outlook, every conversation with anyone outside the company is copied into the CRM, including newsletters, receipts and personal mail. Almost none of it is linked to a person, so it clutters the workspace and exposes private mail to teammates.

## What should happen

Outlook follows the same rule as Gmail. A conversation is stored only when someone on it is already a contact, writes from a CRM company's work domain, or the conversation is already linked. Everything else stays in Outlook.

## Who it hits and how bad

* Every workspace with Outlook connected. On 19 Oct 2026, 9,390 of 9,789 stored Outlook threads (95.9%) had no person attached, across 61 workspaces (read-only replica, all time, not deleted).
* In the last 30 days (19 Sep to 19 Oct 2026) it was 96.3% of 9,230 Outlook threads, against 17.4% of 363,286 for Gmail.
* A customer has reported personal and family email showing in their CRM: ENG-14940. It isn't proven that this report is Outlook, so check it while fixing this.
* The attached file `outlook-affected-workspaces-2026-10-19.md` lists every affected workspace with counts, dates, the Outlook users and the owners, so support can contact them.

## How to see it

1. Connect an Outlook inbox that has outside email to a new workspace with no contacts.
2. Wait for the 90-day import to finish.
3. Open Conversations or the database: outside conversations are stored with no person. With Gmail, the same inbox stores nothing.

Not reproduced on a preview by us yet. The counts above are measured.

## What we know so far

Part of ENG-15711. Gmail got the "only store mail that involves the CRM" rule in ENG-13977, but Outlook never did. Outlook's page saver removes only internal-only conversations and saves the rest. It also ignores the workspace's "New people from email" setting.

Today:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Outlook page of messages] --> B{Internal only?}
  B -- yes --> C[Dropped]
  B -- no --> D[Saved to the CRM]
```

After this change:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Outlook page of messages] --> B{Internal only?}
  B -- yes --> C[Dropped]
  B -- no --> E{NEW: anyone in the CRM?}
  E -- yes --> D[Saved on their record]
  E -- no --> F[NEW: not saved, address indexed]
```

## Split (19 Oct 2026)

Pulling in a contact's past Outlook email when they are added later moved to Show a new contact's past Outlook email on their record, so this fix can ship first. The address index bullet below is for that ticket.

## Done when

- [ ] An Outlook inbox connected to a workspace with no contacts stores 0 conversations.
- [ ] A conversation with a contact on To or CC is stored on that contact.
- [ ] A conversation from someone at a CRM company's work domain is stored.
- [ ] A reply from a new address inside an already stored conversation is stored.
- [ ] The workspace's "New people from email" setting applies to Outlook the same way it applies to Gmail.
- [ ] Already stored Outlook conversations with nobody in the CRM are removed by a cleanup run, with a dry run first that reports the count per workspace.
- [ ] Re-running an import page or a change notification creates no duplicates.
- [ ] Tests cover the Outlook store rule at the page-save seam, red before and green after.

<details><summary>For whoever fixes it</summary>

* Outlook page saver: `apps/web/lib/services/outlook-message-page.ts` (`persistOutlookMessagePage`). The internal-only check and `saveThread` loop sit around lines 554 to 626 on main.
* Gmail rule to reuse: `evaluateGmailThreadMatch` and `loadGmailMatchContextForAddresses` in `apps/web/lib/services/gmail-crm-thread-match.ts`. Gmail page flow for reference: `apps/web/lib/services/gmail-message-page.ts`.
* Address index for later lookups: `integration_mailbox_address_index` is Gmail-shaped today (Gmail message and thread ids). Outlook needs an equivalent or a provider column so a contact added later can find their mail.
* Cleanup to mirror: `apps/web/scripts/purge-unmatched-gmail-mail.ts` and `apps/web/lib/services/gmail-unmatched-mail-purge.ts`.
* Policy: `organization.contact_creation_policy` in `packages/db/src/schema/organization.ts`; creation logic in `apps/web/lib/crm/contact-creation-policy.ts`.
* Live sync path: `apps/web/lib/services/outlook-*` delta processing uses the same page saver.
* Measurement queries: read-only replica, `crm_message_thread` where `outlook_conversation_id is not null`, split by `contact_id is null`.

</details>
